title: Common Heart Medication May Also Lower Dementia Risk
subtitle: New research suggests that starting statins early could help protect the brain as well as the heart.

summary.en: A new 15-year study shows that statins can lower the risk of dementia by up to 15 percent. Researchers tracked over 132,000 people to understand the link between cholesterol medication and brain health. The findings suggest that starting treatment earlier in life is more effective. Experts believe high cholesterol may damage blood vessels that supply the brain. This research adds to growing evidence that heart health and brain health are closely connected.
summary.zh: 一項為期十五年的新研究顯示，史他汀類藥物可將失智症風險降低最高百分之十五。研究人員追蹤了超過十三萬兩千人，以了解膽固醇藥物與大腦健康之間的關聯。研究結果顯示，越早開始治療效果越好。專家認為，高膽固醇可能會損害供應大腦的血管。這項研究進一步證實了心臟健康與大腦健康密切相關的證據。

paragraphs.en: A major new study has provided fresh hope in the fight against dementia. Researchers have found that statins—a common type of medicine used to lower cholesterol—may also help protect the brain. According to The Guardian Health, this 15-year study suggests that people who take these drugs could reduce their risk of developing dementia by as much as 15 percent.
paragraphs.zh: 一項重大的新研究為對抗失智症帶來了新希望。研究人員發現，史他汀類藥物（statins）——一種常用於降低膽固醇的藥物——或許也有助於保護大腦。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，這項為期十五年的研究顯示，服用這類藥物的人，罹患失智症的風險最高可降低百分之十五。

paragraphs.en: This research is particularly important because the number of people living with dementia is expected to grow significantly in the coming years. Experts predict that the number of cases worldwide could nearly triple to 153 million by 2050. However, many scientists believe that nearly half of these cases could be prevented or delayed if people manage certain health risks throughout their lives.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究之所以特別重要，是因為未來幾年失智症患者的人數預計將大幅增加。專家預測，到了二〇五〇年，全球病例數可能增加近三倍，達到一億五千三百萬人。然而，許多科學家認為，如果人們能在生命各階段妥善管理特定的健康風險，近半數的病例是可以預防或延緩發生的。

paragraphs.en: Statins are already widely used around the world to help prevent heart disease. They work by lowering low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol in the blood. High levels of this 'bad' cholesterol can cause plaque—a sticky substance—to build up in the arteries. This buildup can block blood flow, leading to heart attacks or strokes. Scientists now believe that this same process may also damage the blood vessels that supply the brain, which increases the risk of dementia.
paragraphs.zh: 史他汀類藥物目前已在全球廣泛用於預防心臟病。其作用機制是降低血液中的低密度脂蛋白膽固醇。這種「壞」膽固醇濃度過高時，會導致斑塊（一種黏性物質）在動脈中堆積。這些堆積物會阻塞血流，進而引發心臟病發作或中風。科學家現在認為，同樣的過程也可能損害供應大腦的血管，進而增加失智症的風險。

paragraphs.en: To better understand this connection, researchers in Denmark followed more than 132,000 people between 2006 and 2021. All participants in this specific study had type 2 diabetes, a condition that often requires careful health management. The results, which were presented at the annual congress of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and published in the Lancet Regional Health Europe journal, showed clear benefits for those taking the medication.
paragraphs.zh: 為了更深入了解這種關聯，丹麥的研究人員在二〇〇六年到二〇二一年間，追蹤了超過十三萬兩千名受試者。這項研究的所有參與者皆患有第二型糖尿病，這是一種通常需要謹慎進行健康管理的疾病。研究結果已在歐洲心臟學會（European Society of Cardiology, ESC）的年度大會上發表，並刊登於《刺胳針區域健康—歐洲》（The Lancet Regional Health Europe）期刊，顯示服用該藥物對受試者有顯著益處。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Tummas Ternhamar from Copenhagen University Hospital, who presented the findings, explained that the timing of the treatment is very important. According to The Guardian Health, those who started taking statins early in the study period saw a 15 percent lower risk of dementia. Those who began the treatment later still saw a benefit, with a 10 percent reduction in risk. Dr. Ternhamar noted that these results support the idea that doctors should look at several health factors at once, rather than focusing on just one area of the body.
paragraphs.zh: 發表此研究結果的哥本哈根大學醫院（Copenhagen University Hospital）醫師特恩哈馬（Tummas Ternhamar）解釋，治療時機非常關鍵。根據《衛報健康》報導，在研究初期就開始服用史他汀類藥物的人，失智症風險降低了百分之十五；較晚開始治療的人也有所獲益，風險降低了百分之十。特恩哈馬醫師指出，這些結果支持了一種觀點：醫師應同時考量多項健康因素，而非僅關注身體的單一部位。

paragraphs.en: Prof. Isabel Goncalves, a member of the ESC communication committee who was not involved in the research, praised the study. She pointed out that because statins are inexpensive and already available in most parts of the world, these findings could have a major impact on public health. She suggested that the medication could eventually become part of a larger plan to keep people healthy, alongside other habits like eating well and staying physically active.
paragraphs.zh: 未參與此項研究的歐洲心臟學會通訊委員會成員伊莎貝爾·貢薩爾維斯（Isabel Goncalves）教授對該研究給予高度評價。她指出，由於史他汀類藥物價格低廉且全球多數地區皆可取得，這些發現可能對公共衛生產生重大影響。她建議，該藥物最終可能成為維持健康計畫的一部分，並與均衡飲食及保持身體活動等其他習慣相輔相成。

paragraphs.en: This new research follows other recent studies that have highlighted the benefits of statins for different groups. For example, previous reports have shown that the medication can also help healthy people over the age of 70 avoid heart problems. Together, these studies suggest that protecting the heart and the brain often requires the same approach: keeping blood vessels clear and healthy.
paragraphs.zh: 這項新研究延續了近期其他強調史他汀類藥物對不同族群益處的研究。例如，先前的報告顯示，該藥物也能幫助七十歲以上的健康長者避免心臟問題。綜合來看，這些研究顯示保護心臟與大腦通常需要採取相同的方法：保持血管暢通與健康。

paragraphs.en: While the results are promising, experts are still working to find out exactly why statins have this protective effect on the brain. For now, the study adds to the growing list of 'modifiable' risk factors—things we can change or treat—that might help prevent dementia. The Lancet dementia commission has previously suggested that addressing 14 different health factors, starting from childhood, could help prevent or delay 45 percent of dementia cases. Treating high cholesterol from midlife is considered one of the most important steps in that process.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管研究結果令人振奮，專家們仍在努力釐清為何史他汀類藥物對大腦具有這種保護作用。目前，這項研究增加了「可改變」風險因素的清單——即我們能透過改變或治療來預防失智症的事項。刺胳針失智症委員會（The Lancet dementia commission）先前曾建議，從童年開始針對十四種不同的健康因素進行改善，有助於預防或延緩百分之四十五的失智症病例。而在中年時期治療高膽固醇，被視為該過程中最重要的步驟之一。

paragraphs.en: As researchers continue to study the long-term effects of these drugs, the message for patients remains consistent: taking care of your heart health early in life may be one of the best ways to protect your brain as you get older. While more studies will be needed to confirm these results in broader populations, the current evidence offers a hopeful path forward for millions of people around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著研究人員持續探討這些藥物的長期影響，給病患的訊息始終如一：在年輕時照顧好心臟健康，可能是年老後保護大腦的最佳方式之一。雖然還需要更多研究來證實這些結果是否適用於更廣泛的人群，但目前的證據為全球數百萬人提供了一條充滿希望的道路。

quiz.question: According to the study presented by Dr. Tummas Ternhamar, what is the specific difference in dementia risk reduction based on when statin treatment begins?

options.A: Starting early results in a 10 percent reduction, while starting late results in a 15 percent reduction.
options.B: Starting early results in a 15 percent reduction, while starting late results in a 10 percent reduction.
options.C: Starting early results in a 45 percent reduction, while starting late results in a 15 percent reduction.
options.D: There is no difference in risk reduction regardless of when the treatment begins.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 B。根據文章第五段，Dr. Tummas Ternhamar 明確指出，較早開始服用他汀類藥物的人風險降低了 15%，而較晚開始的人則降低了 10%。選項 A 將兩者數值顛倒了；選項 C 混淆了文章後段提到的「45%」數據（該數據是指整體可預防的失智比例，而非單一藥物效果）；選項 D 則與文中提到的時間因素影響直接矛盾。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between heart health and brain health based on the findings in the article?

options.A: Brain health is completely independent of the cardiovascular system.
options.B: Statins only improve brain health if the patient has already suffered a heart attack.
options.C: Maintaining clear blood vessels is beneficial for both the heart and the brain.
options.D: The medication used to treat heart disease is ineffective at preventing dementia in patients with diabetes.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 C。文章第三段提到壞膽固醇會阻塞血管導致心臟問題，且科學家認為同樣的過程也會損害供應大腦的血管，加上第七段總結「保護心臟和保護大腦往往需要相同的方法」，可推論兩者健康息息相關。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 文中並未限制僅限心臟病發患者；選項 D 與第四段提到的研究對象（糖尿病患者）受益的事實矛盾。

quiz.question: In the eighth paragraph, the author refers to 'modifiable' risk factors. What does 'modifiable' mean in this context?

options.A: Factors that can be changed or influenced through action.
options.B: Factors that are impossible to measure or track.
options.C: Factors that are determined entirely by genetics.
options.D: Factors that are currently being studied by scientists.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 A。文中括號解釋了 'modifiable' 即 'things we can change or treat'（我們可以改變或治療的事物）。在醫學語境下，這代表這些風險因子並非不可逆的，而是可以透過生活習慣或藥物介入來改善。選項 B 與文意相反；選項 C 提到的遺傳因素通常是不可改變的；選項 D 雖然文中確實有提到研究，但 'modifiable' 本身的定義是指「可改變性」，而非「研究中」。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding the fight against dementia?

options.A: Statins are a guaranteed cure for all types of dementia if taken early enough.
options.B: The increase in dementia cases is inevitable and cannot be prevented by medical intervention.
options.C: Managing heart health and addressing risk factors early can play a significant role in preventing dementia.
options.D: The cost of statins makes them an impractical solution for the global dementia crisis.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 C。全文主旨圍繞在心臟健康與大腦健康的關聯，並強調透過及早管理膽固醇等風險因子，可以有效降低或延緩失智症的發生。選項 A 過度誇大，文中僅稱「降低風險」而非「保證治癒」；選項 B 與文中提到的「可預防或延緩」觀點矛盾；選項 D 與第六段提到的「statins are inexpensive」（藥物價格低廉）的事實不符。
